human_actions_pending.context: The nginx.conf and Dockerfile changes (gzip_static precompression, immutable cache headers) only take effect on a fresh image build. The deployed bundle is still the old uncompressed one — a 29 MB JS asset with no Cache-Control.

human_actions_pending.action: Verify compression and cache headers through the upstream proxy after deploy
human_actions_pending.context: All measurements were taken against the container on localhost:5174. If the proxy strips Accept-Encoding or injects its own Cache-Control, none of the gains reach users. Command: curl -sI -u eti -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' https://cheminfo.beilstein.org/explain-that-inchi/<asset-from-deployed-index> | grep -iE '^(HTTP|content-length|content-type|content-encoding|cache-control)'

human_actions_pending.action: Confirm log rotation is <= 14 days on the host
human_actions_pending.context: Privacy policy § 2 (2) promises log deletion within 2 weeks. Nothing in the repo enforces this — nginx.conf defines no access_log directive, so it inherits the base image default and retention is a logrotate concern on the server. The claim is unbacked until someone confirms it.

human_actions_pending.action: Report back to the DPO/reviewer on two points
human_actions_pending.context: Their feedback was written against a pre-872b1ff version. (a) § 3 (3) no longer exists — it described a Service Worker that never registers now that COOP/COEP come from the origin. (b) The § 2 (4) comment appears aimed at § 3 (2); § 2 (4) never described local storage. Next review round should be against current text.

human_actions_pending.action: Remove the temporary password protection when ready to launch
human_actions_pending.context: Site is gated at an upstream proxy. Until it is removed, og:image/canonical will not unfurl in Slack/Teams/social and search engines cannot index — scrapers receive 401. This is expected, not a bug in the URL swap.

decisions.rationale: nginx sets COOP/COEP at the origin and the proxy passes both through (verified via curl), so coi-serviceworker.js returns early at line 110 and never registers. The paragraph described a code path that cannot execute on this deployment.

decisions.decision: Precompress at image build with gzip -9 + gzip_static, rather than runtime gzip alone
decisions.rationale: The largest chunk is 21 MB minified and content-hashed, so its bytes never change. Runtime-gzipping it per cold request costs ~1-2s CPU each time for an identical result. Runtime gzip stays on as a fallback for anything without a .gz sibling.
Keeps WASM streaming compilation undisturbed. The two Indigo files are served as-is.

decisions.decision: Repeated COOP/COEP inside every new nginx location block
decisions.rationale: nginx add_header does not inherit into a block that declares its own. Omitting them would silently strip cross-origin isolation from JS and WASM and break SharedArrayBuffer, i.e. break InChI computation.

decisions.decision: Moved the title rule from h2 border-top to h1 border-bottom
decisions.rationale: The h2 rule was a section separator; a rule appeared under the title only on Privacy, where an h2 directly follows the h1. Giving the h1 its own rule makes all three docs open identically and decouples the look from how a document happens to start.

decisions.decision: Kept the footer Licenses removal without losing attribution
decisions.rationale: TERMS_HTML carries a 'Third-party components' section in-app, and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md remains at the repo root, so MIT/BSD notice obligations still have an in-app path.

decisions.decision: Did not add Playwright as a project dependency for OG image rasterizing
decisions.rationale: Once-a-year task. Rendered via the already-cached Playwright chromium and a throwaway script in scratchpad; documented the requirement in the index.html comment instead.

decisions.decision: Auto-delete editor localStorage on leaving, sweeping by 'ketcher' prefix
decisions.rationale: User chose maximum data minimisation over persistence after being shown the trade-off. Prefix sweep rather than a key list because Ketcher renames keys across versions and a stale list would leave data behind that the privacy policy claims is deleted. Accepted cost: saved favourite structures do not survive a visit.

next_action: Rebuild and redeploy the container so the nginx compression and cache-header changes reach users, then re-run the compression check through the proxy against a real deployed asset name.
